vision.one_liner: Open-source fleet management for small businesses — see your vehicles, track your maintenance, own your data.
vision.tagline: Fleet management that doesn't charge you per van.

target_audience.primary: Small business owners with 5-50 light commercial vehicles
target_audience.persona: Owner-operator who manages the fleet themselves alongside 12 other jobs

differentiators: Open source — no per-vehicle SaaS fees
Self-hosted — your data stays on your server
No hardware lock-in — works with any GPS source
Simple UX — designed for owner-operators, not enterprise fleet managers
Built-in simulator — try it without owning a fleet
vision.competitive_positioning: Nextcloud for fleet management. Credible open-source alternative that gives small operators enterprise-grade capability without enterprise pricing or complexity.

FA1.name: Fleet Dashboard & Live Map

user_journeys.name: View live fleet map
user_journeys.steps: Owner opens app → sees live map with all vehicle positions → vehicles color-coded by traffic light status (green/orange/red) and motion state (moving/idle/parked)

user_journeys.name: Inspect vehicle from map
user_journeys.steps: Owner clicks vehicle marker on map → popup shows vehicle name, driver, status, speed, last trip, traffic light, any alerts → link to full vehicle detail view

user_journeys.name: Review fleet status sidebar
user_journeys.steps: Owner glances at sidebar → sees vehicles due for service (count + list), overdue inspections, expiring documents, active alerts sorted by urgency

user_journeys.name: Filter map by status
user_journeys.steps: Owner filters map → by traffic light status, by driver, by motion state (moving/idle/parked)

acceptance_criteria: Map loads in <2s with 50 vehicle markers
Vehicle positions update in real-time via WebSocket (<5s latency)
Vehicle markers show direction of travel when moving
Vehicle markers color-coded by traffic light status
Sidebar shows top-priority alerts sorted by urgency
Map remembers zoom level and center between sessions
Responsive: usable on tablet with sidebar collapsing to bottom sheet
Clicking vehicle marker opens popup with key stats and link to detail
Map clusters markers at low zoom levels

FA2.name: Vehicle Registry & Detail View

user_journeys.name: Add a vehicle
user_journeys.steps: Owner clicks Add Vehicle → enters make, model, year, VIN, license plate, color, current odometer, photo → saves

user_journeys.name: View vehicle detail
user_journeys.steps: Owner opens vehicle from list or map → sees tabbed view with Overview, Trips, Maintenance, Inspections, Documents

user_journeys.name: Check vehicle health at a glance
user_journeys.steps: Overview tab shows traffic light indicator, current location on mini-map, assigned driver, odometer, key stats

user_journeys.name: Change vehicle status
user_journeys.steps: Owner edits vehicle status → active, in-shop, decommissioned → decommissioned vehicles hidden from map/dashboard by default

acceptance_criteria: Vehicle list supports search, sort (name, status, mileage, next service), and filter
Vehicle list shows traffic light indicator per row (worst status across maintenance, inspections, documents)
Vehicle detail loads all tabs without page refresh
Traffic light: green = all clear, orange = requires attention, red = overdue/compliance failure
Vehicle photo upload supported
Decommissioned vehicles hidden from map and dashboard by default, visible via filter
Vehicle detail overview shows mini-map with current position

FA3.name: GPS Ingestion, Trip Detection & Simulator

user_journeys.name: Simulator feeds fleet data
user_journeys.steps: Simulator service runs → generates realistic GPS coordinates for N configured vehicles → POSTs to ingestion API → vehicles appear on map moving along roads

user_journeys.name: System detects trip start
user_journeys.steps: Vehicle moves >5km/h for >30s → system creates trip record → trip appears in vehicle's trip list as 'active'

user_journeys.name: System detects trip end
user_journeys.steps: Vehicle stationary for >3min → system closes trip → calculates distance (from GPS points, not straight-line) and duration

user_journeys.name: View trip on map
user_journeys.steps: Owner opens vehicle → Trips tab → clicks trip → sees route line on map with start/end markers, timestamps, distance, duration

user_journeys.name: Browse trip history
user_journeys.steps: Owner views trip list for a vehicle → filters by date range → sorts by distance or duration

acceptance_criteria: GPS ingestion API: POST endpoint accepting lat, lon, speed, heading, timestamp, vehicle_id
Positions stored with PostGIS geometry type
Trip detection runs as background process, <30s from trip end to record creation
Trip start threshold: speed >5km/h for >30s (configurable)
Trip end threshold: stationary for >3min (configurable)
Minimum trip distance: 200m to filter GPS drift (configurable)
Trip distance calculated from actual GPS points along route
Trip route rendered as polyline on map with start/end markers
Simulator configurable: number of vehicles, speed profiles, trip patterns
Simulator generates routes that follow roads (not random straight lines)
Simulator runs as a Docker Compose service alongside app and db

FA4.name: Maintenance & Service Management

user_journeys.name: Create service schedule
user_journeys.steps: Owner creates service schedule for a vehicle → selects type (oil change, tires, brakes...) → sets interval by mileage OR time OR both → sets estimated cost

user_journeys.name: Receive service alert
user_journeys.steps: System detects service approaching threshold (e.g., 500mi before due, 2 weeks before) → alert appears on dashboard sidebar and vehicle detail

user_journeys.name: Log completed service
user_journeys.steps: Owner logs service → date, odometer, cost, vendor, notes, receipt photo → service record added to history → next service due recalculated

user_journeys.name: View maintenance history
user_journeys.steps: Owner opens vehicle → Maintenance tab → sees chronological history filterable by type → running cost total

user_journeys.name: Fleet-wide maintenance overview
user_journeys.steps: Owner opens Maintenance from sidebar → sees what's due this week/month across all vehicles → sorted by urgency

acceptance_criteria: Service schedules support mileage-based, time-based, or dual triggers
Alerts fire at configurable warning thresholds (e.g., 500mi before, 2 weeks before)
Maintenance cost tracking with per-vehicle and fleet-wide totals
Common service types pre-populated (oil, tires, brakes, filters, fluids, belts, battery)
Custom service types supported
Receipt photo upload on service records
Completed service resets the schedule countdown automatically

FA5.name: Driver Management & Auth

user_journeys.name: Create driver profile
user_journeys.steps: Owner creates driver → name, phone, email, license number, license expiry, photo → driver receives login credentials

user_journeys.name: Assign driver to vehicle (assigned model)
user_journeys.steps: Owner assigns driver to vehicle → one driver per vehicle at a time → assignment history tracked

user_journeys.name: Driver logs in (assigned model)
user_journeys.steps: Driver logs in → sees their assigned vehicle → current status, next service due, pending inspections → tracking-active indicator visible

user_journeys.name: Driver checks into pool vehicle
user_journeys.steps: Driver logs in → sees available vehicles list → picks one → system creates temporal assignment → pre-trip inspection prompted

user_journeys.name: View driver history
user_journeys.steps: Owner opens driver detail → sees all vehicles they've driven, duration per vehicle, assignment history

acceptance_criteria: Two roles: admin (owner/manager) and driver
Driver sees only their assigned vehicle(s)
Assignment history tracked with timestamps (who drove what, when)
License expiry alerts surface on dashboard and driver list
Driver login works on mobile browser (responsive)
Pool mode: driver selects from available vehicles, temporal assignment created
Assigned mode: driver sees their primary vehicle on login
First-login privacy notice shown and must be acknowledged before tracking begins
Tracking-active indicator visible in driver UI at all times when tracking is on
End-shift toggle available to driver — stops tracking until next shift
Tracking schedule configurable by admin (e.g., 07:00-18:00 Mon-Fri) — on by default
Per-driver data export (JSON/CSV) for GDPR right of access
Per-driver data hard delete for GDPR right to erasure

FA6.name: Inspections & Compliance

user_journeys.name: Create inspection template
user_journeys.steps: Owner creates template → name, list of check items (tires, lights, brakes, fluids, seatbelt...) → assigns to vehicle type

user_journeys.name: Driver completes pre-trip inspection
user_journeys.steps: Driver opens inspection → sees checklist → marks each item pass/fail/NA → adds notes and photos for failures → submits

user_journeys.name: Admin reviews inspections
user_journeys.steps: Owner views inspections → sees pass rate, outstanding failures → clicks inspection to see detail with photos

user_journeys.name: Compliance tracking
user_journeys.steps: System tracks inspection frequency per vehicle → alerts if vehicle hasn't been inspected on schedule → compliance view shows current/overdue status

acceptance_criteria: Customizable checklist templates with different templates per vehicle type
Photo attachment on failed inspection items
Inspection history per vehicle with pass/fail summary
Compliance view: which vehicles are current vs overdue on inspections
Inspection submissions timestamped and immutable (audit trail)
Inspection frequency alerts configurable (e.g., daily pre-trip required)
Disclaimer: not a tachograph, ELD, or DVIR-compliant system

factory_decisions.decision: Client-side tab switching with useState instead of URL-based routing
factory_decisions.context: AC says 'loads all tabs without page refresh' — need client-side tab mechanism
alternatives_considered: URL hash-based tabs (#overview, #trips) — provides bookmarkable URLs but adds complexity
Next.js parallel routes — over-engineered for placeholder tabs
factory_decisions.rationale: Simple useState tab switching is the boring technology choice (McKinley). Tabs share the same data context (vehicle object) so no data fetching needed on switch. Proper ARIA roles (tablist, tab, tabpanel) for accessibility. Can evolve to URL-based later when tabs have real content.

factory_decisions.decision: Decommissioned filtering moved from server to client in vehicle list
factory_decisions.context: AC says 'visible via filter' — need toggle mechanism. Server was filtering out DECOMMISSIONED in the Supabase query.
alternatives_considered: URL search param (?showDecommissioned=true) with server-side filtering — adds page reload
Keep server filter, add separate API call on toggle — unnecessary network round-trip for 5-50 vehicles
factory_decisions.rationale: Fleet is 5-50 vehicles (per vision). Client-side filtering is instant and consistent with existing search/sort/filter pattern in VehicleList. Toggle checkbox hidden when no decommissioned vehicles exist. Dashboard map keeps server-side exclusion (no toggle needed on map).

factory_decisions.decision: VehicleMiniMap is a separate non-interactive component from FleetMap
factory_decisions.context: Overview tab needs a mini-map showing single vehicle position
alternatives_considered: Reuse FleetMap with single vehicle array — rejected because FleetMap has clustering, click handlers, persistence, and other features unnecessary for a static mini-map
Embed FleetMap with a 'mini' prop — rejected because it couples the two use cases
factory_decisions.rationale: VehicleMiniMap is a focused component: non-interactive (interactive: false), no clustering, no popups, no persistence. Single Marker for the vehicle, color-coded by traffic light. Reuses the same CartoDB Positron tile source. ~60 lines vs FleetMap's 230 lines. Separate concerns, no coupling.

architecture.notes: Clean separation: lib/ for pure logic, hooks/ for state, components/ for presentation, api/ for routes. Dependency direction is correct — components depend on lib, not vice versa. Server components (dashboard page) fetch data and pass to client components. Supabase proxy in db.ts is clever but uses a non-standard pattern that could confuse contributors. Position event emitter uses Node EventEmitter which won't scale beyond a single process — acceptable for v1 but will need Redis/Supabase Realtime for production multi-instance.

consistency.notes: Consistent naming (camelCase props, snake_case DB columns with explicit mapping). File structure follows Next.js conventions. API routes consistently use NextResponse, Zod validation, and error shapes. Minor inconsistency: dashboard page.tsx uses inline type assertions instead of shared types from vehicles.ts.

robustness.notes: Good null coalescing throughout (?? operators). SSE stream has proper cleanup (abort listener, clearInterval, unsubscribe). Error boundary wraps map. localStorage access guarded with try/catch. Position ingestion validates vehicle existence. Edge case: dashboard fetches ALL positions ordered by timestamp to find latest per vehicle — will degrade with data growth (needs DISTINCT ON or a latest_position materialized view).

production_risks.notes: console.error calls in API routes are acceptable for server-side logging but should use a structured logger in production. No request body size limits on POST /api/positions — a malicious client could send an unbounded array. EventEmitter-based SSE will not work across multiple server instances. The positions query in dashboard page fetches all positions for all vehicles to find the latest — this is an N+1 concern that will become a performance bottleneck. No timeout on Supabase queries.

security.notes: CRITICAL: POST /api/positions has NO authentication — anyone can submit fake GPS data for any vehicle. GET /api/vehicles has NO authentication — fleet data (names, plates, locations) is publicly accessible. GET /api/positions/stream has NO authentication — SSE stream of all vehicle movements is public. Login route uses select('*') which fetches the password_hash column (needed for verification but wider than necessary). No rate limiting on any endpoint. No CSRF protection on position ingestion. HTML in popup is properly escaped via escapeHTML().

dead_hallucinated_code.notes: No unused imports detected. All exported functions are consumed. The 'idle' tripState in simulator never triggers (transitions go parked→driving→parked). PositionUpdate type is duplicated between position-events.ts and use-realtime-vehicles.ts — not dead code but could share a single definition.

tech_debt.notes: Inline type assertions in dashboard page (e.g., 'as GREEN | ORANGE | RED') instead of deriving from Prisma or shared types. Supabase client used directly instead of through a repository pattern — acceptable for project size but will create coupling if it grows. The positionBatchSchema validator is separate from the Prisma schema — drift risk. EventEmitter for pub/sub is a single-process limitation that will need rework.

code_review_report.evaluator_observations: TypeScript compiles cleanly with zero errors. ESLint is not configured. Code architecture is clean with good separation of concerns — server components for data fetching, client components for interactivity, pure utility functions in lib/. The SSE-based real-time update pipeline (EventEmitter → ReadableStream → EventSource hook) is well-implemented for single-process deployment. The most significant issue is the complete absence of authentication on three data API routes (vehicles list, position ingestion, position stream), which means anyone with the URL can read fleet locations and inject fake GPS data. This is the single highest-priority fix needed before any production use. Secondary concerns: the positions query pattern (fetch all, filter in JS) will not scale, and the EventEmitter pub/sub is process-local. Overall code quality is solid for a cycle-1 product — the auth gaps are the only blocking issue.

root_cause_analysis.gap_description: No UI exists to change vehicle status (FA2-J4). Users cannot mark vehicles as requiring attention, decommission them, or update any vehicle fields. The status display is read-only with no edit affordance.
root_cause_analysis.evidence: FA2-J4 is a specified journey ('Owner edits vehicle status → active, in-shop, decommissioned') but the story decomposition created only 3 stories (vehicle-list, add-vehicle, vehicle-detail) covering FA2-J1, FA2-J2, and FA2-J3. FA2-J4 was never assigned a story. The builder built all 3 stories they were given correctly. The decommissioned filter toggle (factory_decision: client-side filtering) correctly shows/hides decommissioned vehicles, but there is no way to SET a vehicle to decommissioned status. Root cause is upstream: the decomposition phase missed a journey.
root_cause_analysis.related_factory_decision: Decommissioned filtering moved from server to client in vehicle list — builder implemented the filter side but was never asked to build the status-change side

root_cause_analysis.gap_description: Vehicle photo is uploaded during add-vehicle but never displayed on the vehicle detail page. photoUrl is fetched from DB and mapped but not rendered. Broken feature promise.
root_cause_analysis.evidence: The add-vehicle form accepts photo upload and stores photoUrl in the database. The GET /api/vehicles/[id] route fetches photoUrl and maps it to camelCase. The VehicleDetail component receives the data but never renders the photo. The spec says 'Vehicle photo upload supported' — upload works, but display was missed. The factory_decision 'Search Before Building' audit identified photo as part of the vehicle-detail scope. No factory_question about whether to display the photo. A different builder would likely have made the same mistake only if they interpreted 'upload supported' narrowly as the upload action alone.
root_cause_analysis.related_factory_decision: Search Before Building audit — listed vehicle detail page as BUILD scope, photo was part of add-vehicle story scope

root_cause_analysis.gap_description: No success feedback after adding a vehicle. Silent redirect to list.
root_cause_analysis.evidence: The FA2-J1 journey says 'enters make, model, year... → saves'. The word 'saves' implies persistence but doesn't specify user feedback on success. This matches the cross-cycle pattern from dashboard-features: spec describes actions but not feedback patterns. The builder implemented router.push('/vehicles') after successful POST, which is correct behavior but lacks user confirmation. Standard UX practice includes a success toast, but the spec doesn't mention toasts anywhere in FA2.

root_cause_analysis.gap_description: Photo upload failure silently swallowed. Vehicle created without photo, no warning.
root_cause_analysis.evidence: The add-vehicle form catches upload errors but doesn't surface them to the user — the vehicle is saved without a photo and the user is redirected to the list with no indication the upload failed. Error handling for partial failures is a basic engineering practice that doesn't need spec-level instructions. The vehicle should either retry the upload, show a warning, or at minimum surface a notification that the photo wasn't saved.

root_cause_analysis.gap_description: Traffic light in vehicle list is color-only (8x8px dot) with no text label or tooltip. Insufficient for color-blind users.
root_cause_analysis.evidence: The dashboard already has an accessible TrafficLight component (role=status, descriptive aria-labels) from the dashboard-features milestone. The factory_decision 'Search Before Building' explicitly identified 'REUSE (TrafficLight component)' as available. The builder chose a minimal 8x8px dot representation for the list view instead of reusing or adapting the existing TrafficLight component. This is a design judgment call — compact list views often use minimal indicators — but it breaks the accessibility contract established by the dashboard's traffic light implementation.
root_cause_analysis.related_factory_decision: Search Before Building audit — listed TrafficLight component as REUSE candidate

root_cause_analysis.gap_description: No fleet health summary on the list page. Owner must scan every row to assess fleet condition.
root_cause_analysis.evidence: The FA2 spec says 'Vehicle list supports search, sort, filter' and 'shows traffic light indicator per row' — no mention of a summary bar or aggregate health view. The dashboard (FA1-J3) has a 4-column vehicle count grid (Total/OK/Attention/Overdue), but FA2 has no equivalent journey for fleet-wide summary on the list page. The PO correctly identifies this as a gap — a plumber with 8 vans wants to glance at fleet health without scanning rows — but the spec didn't call it out.

root_cause_analysis.gap_description: Required vs optional fields not visually distinguished in add-vehicle form.
root_cause_analysis.evidence: Distinguishing required from optional form fields is a standard UX pattern (WAI-ARIA form guidance recommends asterisk or '(optional)' suffix). The Zod validation schema defines which fields are required, so the data model supports the distinction. The builder simply didn't add visual indicators. No spec instruction needed for this — it's a basic form design pattern.

phase_decisions.decision: XSS recurrence pattern: same vulnerability type as fix-qa-xss-popup, different code path
